title: 集灭随观
note: 见身受心法、蕴处受的集起与灭去

evidence.pali: 5 . Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘samādhiṃ, bhikkhave, bhāvetha; samāhito, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Kiñca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti? Rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca , saññāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saṅkhārānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca’’.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 5. 如是我闻：一时，世尊住在舍卫城祇陀林给孤独园。当时，世尊对比丘们说：‘诸比丘！’‘尊者！’那些比丘回答世尊。世尊说：‘诸比丘，当修习定。诸比丘，得定之比丘能如实了知。如实了知什么呢？色之集与灭，受之集与灭，想之集与灭，行之集与灭，识之集与灭。’”
evidence.english: 5. Thus I have heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, develop concentration. A concentrated bhikkhu, bhikkhus, understands things as they really are. And what does he understand as it really is? The origin and passing away of form, the origin and passing away of feeling, the origin and passing away of perception, the origin and passing away of formations, the origin and passing away of consciousness.”

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: 355 . Idāni tadanantare satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅge cattāro ti gaṇanaparicchedo. Tena na tato heṭṭhā na uddhanti satipaṭṭhānaparicchedaṃ dīpeti. Satipaṭṭhānā ti tayo satipaṭṭhānā – satigocaropi, tidhā paṭipannesu sāvakesu satthuno paṭidhānunayavītivattatāpi, satipi. ‘‘Catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… ko ca, bhikkhave, kāyassa samudayo? Āhārasamudayā kāyassa samudayo’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 5.408) hi satigocaro satipaṭṭhānanti vuccati. Tathā ‘‘kāyo upaṭṭhānaṃ, no sati. Sati upaṭṭhānañceva sati cā’’tiādīsu (paṭi. ma. 3.35). Tassattho – patiṭṭhāti asminti paṭṭhānaṃ. Kā patiṭṭhāti? Sati. Satiyā paṭṭhānaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, padhānaṃ ṭhānanti vā paṭṭhānaṃ; satiyā paṭṭhānaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ hatthiṭṭhānaassaṭṭhānādīni viya.
entries.chinese_simplified: 355. 现在，在其后的念处分别(Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga)中，‘四’是数量的限定。以此阐明念处的界限，不多也不少。念处有三：念的行境(satigocara)；导师对三类行道弟子(sāvaka)施教方法(paṭidhānunaya)的超越(vītivattatā)；以及念(sati)本身。如经中所说：‘诸比丘，我将为你们宣说四念处的生起与灭没。你们要谛听……诸比丘，什么是身的生起？由食的生起而有身的生起’等等，于此，念的行境被称为念处。又如‘身是现起处(upaṭṭhāna)，非念；念既是现起处，也是念’等等。其义为：于此建立(patiṭṭhāti)，故为‘处’(paṭṭhāna)。什么于此建立？念。念之处为念处。或，主要之立足处为处；念之处为念处，犹如象栏、马厩等。
entries.english: 355. Now, immediately following that, in the Exposition of the Foundations of Mindfulness, is the section on the enumeration, ‘four.’ By this, it indicates the delimitation of the foundations of mindfulness as neither fewer nor more. As to ‘foundations of mindfulness,’ there are three kinds of ‘foundations of mindfulness’: the domain of mindfulness, the Teacher’s transcending of aversion and attachment in disciples who practice in three ways, and mindfulness itself. For in such passages as, “Monks, I will teach the arising and the passing away of the four foundations of mindfulness. Listen to that… What, monks, is the arising of the body? With the arising of nutriment, there is the arising of the body,” the domain of mindfulness is called a ‘foundation of mindfulness.’ Similarly, in such passages as, “The body is an establishment, not mindfulness. Mindfulness is both an establishment and mindfulness.” The meaning of that is: that in which one stands firm is a foundation (paṭṭhāna). What stands firm? Mindfulness. The foundation of mindfulness is satipaṭṭhāna. Or, a foundation is a principal standing place; the foundation of mindfulness is satipaṭṭhāna, like the standing place of an elephant, the standing place of a horse, and so on.

entries.pali: 301 . Idāni satipaṭṭhānakathā hoti. ‘‘Tattha – catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.408) satipaṭṭhānasaṃyutte vuttanayeneva yesaṃ kāyādayo satiyā ārammaṇadhamme gahetvā ‘‘sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānā’’ti laddhi, seyyathāpi etarahi andhakānaṃ. Andhakā nāma pubbaseliyā, aparaseliyā, rājagiriyā, siddhatthikāti ime pacchā uppannanikāyā. Tesaṃ laddhivivecanatthaṃ pucchā sakavādissa, paṭiññā paravādissa. Tattha yasmā ‘‘patiṭṭhāti etesūti paṭṭhānā . Kā patiṭṭhāti? Sati. Satiyā paṭṭhānā satipaṭṭhānā’’ ti iminā atthena satigocarāpi satipaṭṭhānā. ‘‘Patiṭṭhahantīti paṭṭhānā . Kā patiṭṭhahanti? Satiyo. Satiyova paṭṭhānā satipaṭṭhānā’’ti iminā atthena satiyova satipaṭṭhānā. Tasmā dve pi vādā pariyāyena yujjanti. Ye pana taṃ pariyāyaṃ pahāya ekanteneva ‘‘sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānā’’ti vadanti, te sandhāya pucchā sakavādissa, ārammaṇavasena paṭiññā paravādissa. Sabbe dhammā satī ti anuyuttassa pana sabbesaṃ satisabhāvābhāvato paṭikkhepo tasseva. Tattha khayagāmī tiādīni maggavisesanāni. Ekāyanamaggo hi kilesānaṃ khayabhūtaṃ nibbānaṃ gacchatīti khayagāmī . Cattāri saccāni bujjhanto gacchatīti bodhagāmī . Vaṭṭaṃ apacinanto gacchatīti apacayagāmī . Evametehi padehi ‘‘kiṃ te sabbe dhammā evarūpo te ekāyano maggo hotī’’ti pucchati. Anāsavā asaṃyojaniyā tiādīnipi lokuttarabhāvaṃ pucchanatthāya vuttāni. Buddhānussatī tiādīni pabhedapucchāvasena vuttāni.
entries.chinese_simplified: 301. 现在是念住论。正如在念住相应中所说：‘诸比丘，我将为你们宣说四念住的生起与灭没。’(《相应部》5.408)有些人的观点是‘一切法都是念住’，他们将身等作为念的所缘法，例如现在的安达迦派(Andhakā)。安达迦派即东山部(Pubbaseliyā)、西山部(Aparaseliyā)、王山部(Rājagiriyā)、义成部(Siddhatthikā)，这些是后来生起的部派。为了辨析他们的观点，由本论者提问，由他论者提出主张。于此，从‘于此中安住，故为处。什么安住？念。念之处，故为念住’的意义上说，念的所缘也是念住。从‘能安住，故为处。什么能安住？诸念。念即是处，故为念住’的意义上说，唯念本身是念住。因此，两种说法从不同角度看都是成立的。但对于那些舍弃此种善巧方便而决断地说‘一切法都是念住’的人，本论者针对他们提问，他论者则依所缘的立场作出回答。而对于‘一切法即是念’的主张，则因并非一切法都具有念的自性而予以驳斥。其中，‘导向灭尽’等是道的特质。一乘道朝向诸烦恼灭尽的涅槃而行，故为‘导向灭尽’；觉悟四谛而行，故为‘导向菩提’；减损轮回而行，故为‘导向损减’。通过这些词句提问：‘对你而言，一切法都是这样的一乘道吗？’‘无漏’、‘非结缚’等语，是为了探问其出世间性而说的。‘佛随念’等，则是为了就其类别进行提问而说的。
entries.english: 301. Now there is the discussion on the foundations of mindfulness. Therein—'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the arising and passing away of the four foundations of mindfulness' (SN 5.408). In accordance with the method stated in the Satipaṭṭhāna Saṃyutta, there is the view of those who, taking the body and so forth as the objective phenomena for mindfulness, hold that 'all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness,' such as the Andhakas nowadays. The Andhakas are the later schools, namely, the Pubbaseliyas, Aparaseliyas, Rājagiriyas, and Siddhatthikas. For the purpose of analyzing their view, the question is from the proponent, and the assertion is from the opponent. Herein, because 'one is established in these, thus they are foundations (paṭṭhānā). What is established? Mindfulness (sati). The foundations for mindfulness are the foundations of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhānā)'—by this meaning, even the objects of mindfulness are foundations of mindfulness. 'They are established, thus they are foundations. What are established? Mindfulnesses (satiyo). Mindfulnesses themselves are the foundations, thus foundations of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhānā)'—by this meaning, mindfulnesses themselves are the foundations of mindfulness. Therefore, both views are tenable by way of interpretation. But those who abandon that interpretation and categorically state that 'all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness'—with reference to them, the question is from the proponent, and the assertion, by way of the object, is from the opponent. However, for one who is questioned, 'Are all phenomena mindfulness?', the refutation is for that very one, due to the absence of the nature of mindfulness in all things. Herein, 'leading to destruction' and so forth are qualifiers of the path. For the one-way path goes to Nibbāna, which is the destruction of the defilements; thus it is 'leading to destruction.' It goes while awakening to the four truths; thus it is 'leading to awakening.' It goes while diminishing the round; thus it is 'leading to diminution.' Thus, with these terms, he asks: 'Are all those phenomena for you such a one-way path?' Terms like 'taintless,' 'not connected with the fetters,' and so forth, are also stated for the purpose of asking about the supramundane state. 'Recollection of the Buddha,' and so forth, are stated by way of asking about the classifications.

entries.pali: 413 . Itī ti evaṃ vuttappakārenāti attho. Tena ‘‘so evaṃ samāhite citte’’tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.244-245; ma. ni. 1.384, 431-433; pārā. 12-14) yathādassitapāḷigatiṃ, tassā atthavivaraṇanayañca paccāmasati. Saccesu viya ariyasaccāni khandhesu upādānakkhandhā antogadhā. Tadubhaye ca sabhāvato, samudayato, atthaṅgamato, assādato, ādīnavato, nissaraṇato ca yathābhūtaṃ sayambhuñāṇena avedi aññāsi paṭivijjhi pavedesi vāti sātisayena pañcakkhandhāvabodhena bhagavāva thometabboti āha ‘‘pañcakkhandhavidū’’ ti. Ñatvā viññeyyāti sambandho. Tāsū ti pañcasu abhiññāsu. Taggahaṇeneva ca paribhaṇḍañāṇānaṃ gahitattā ‘‘pañcā’’ti vuttaṃ. Tenāha ‘‘etāsu hī’’ tiādi.
entries.chinese_simplified: 413. “如是”(iti)意即“以如是所说的方式”。他借此省察所开示的巴利文句及其义理阐释的方法，如“彼于如是等持之心……”等（《长部》1.244-245；《中部》1.384, 431-433；《波罗夷》12-14）。如同圣谛包含在诸谛中，取蕴也包含在诸蕴中。并且，对于这两者，从其自性、集、灭、味、患、离，他以无师自通的智慧如实地了知、识知、证知、阐明，因此，以其对五蕴的超胜觉悟，世尊应受赞叹，故说为“五蕴的了知者”(pañcakkhandhavidū)。“了知”与“应被知者”相关联。“于彼等”(tāsu)是指于五神通中。由于此词的涵摄也包含了附属的诸智，因此说“五”。所以说“于此等中……”等。
entries.english: 413. The word iti means 'in the manner thus described.' By this, with the phrase 'when his mind is thus concentrated,' and so on (Dī. Ni. 1.244–245; Ma. Ni. 1.384, 431–433; Pārā. 12–14), one considers the course of the Pāḷi as shown and its method of explaining the meaning. Just as the Noble Truths are included among truths, so too the aggregates of clinging are included within the aggregates. And he knew, understood, penetrated, and taught both of these according to reality with self-originated knowledge in terms of their nature, origin, cessation, gratification, danger, and escape. Therefore, because of his pre-eminent comprehension of the five aggregates, the Blessed One alone is to be praised; thus, it is said, 'knower of the five aggregates.' The connection is: 'having known, they are to be understood.' Tāsu means 'in the five direct knowledges.' And because the auxiliary knowledges are included by the very taking up of those, 'five' is stated. Therefore, it is said: 'for in these,' and so on.

entries.pali: ‘‘Aniccā’’ ti iminā saṅkhāradukkhatāvasena upekkhāvedanāya, sabbavedanāsuyeva vā ādīnavamāha, itarehi itaradukkhatāvasena yathākkamaṃ dukkhasukhavedanānaṃ, avisesena vā tīṇipi padāni sabbāsampi vedanānaṃ vasena yojetabbāni. Aya nti yo vedanāya hutvā abhāvaṭṭhena aniccabhāvo, udayabbayapaṭipīḷanaṭṭhena dukkhabhāvo, jarāya maraṇena cāti dvedhā vipariṇāmetabbabhāvo ca, ayaṃ vedanāya ādīnavo, yato vā ādīnaṃ paramakāruññaṃ vāti pavattatīti. Vedanāya nissaraṇa nti ettha vedanāyā ti nissakkavacanaṃ, yāva vedanāpaṭibaddhaṃ chandarāgaṃ na pajahati, tāvāyaṃ puriso vedanaṃ allīnoyeva hoti. Yadā pana taṃ chandarāgaṃ pajahati, tadāyaṃ puriso vedanāya nissaṭo visaṃyutto hotīti chandarāgappahānaṃ vedanāya nissaraṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Ettha ca vedanāggahaṇena vedanāya sahajātanissayārammaṇabhūtā ca rūpārūpadhammā gahitā eva hontīti pañcannampi upādānakkhandhānaṃ gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vedanāsīsena pana desanā āgatā, tattha kāraṇaṃ vuttameva, lakkhaṇahāranayena vā ayamattho vibhāvetabbo. Tattha vedanāggahaṇena gahitā pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhasaccaṃ, vedanānaṃ samudayaggahaṇena gahitā avijjādayo samudayasaccaṃ, atthaṅgamanissaraṇapariyāyehi nirodhasaccaṃ, ‘‘yathābhūtaṃ viditvā’’ti etena maggasaccanti evamettha cattāri saccāni veditabbāni. Kāmupādānamūlakattā sesupādānānaṃ, pahīne ca kāmupādāne upādānasesābhāvato ‘‘vigatachandarāgatāya anupādāno’’ ti vuttaṃ. Anupādāvimutto ti attano maggaphalappattiṃ bhagavā dasseti. ‘‘Vedanāna’’ntiādinā hi yassā dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā imaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ sakāraṇaṃ sagatikaṃ pabhedato vibhajituṃ samattho ahosi , tassa sabbaññutaññāṇassa saddhiṃ pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya uppattibhūmiṃ dasseti dhammarājā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 以‘无常’一词，是依行苦说舍受的过患，或说一切感受的过患。其余的（苦受和乐受）则依次依其他苦（苦苦和坏苦）而说。或者，这三个词亦可不加区别地应用于所有感受。此即：感受有而后无，义为无常性；为生灭所逼迫，义为苦性；以及为老、死二者所变坏之性——此即感受的过患。或因其极可悲悯而流转。于‘受之出离’中，‘从受’是出离语：只要未断除与感受相关的欲贪，此人便仍执着于感受；唯有断除该欲贪时，此人方从感受中出离、不相应——故说断除欲贪即是感受的出离。此处，以‘受’一词，已同时摄取了与感受俱生、为所依、为所缘的色法和无色法，当知即是摄取了五取蕴。然而，教法是以感受为首而宣说的，其缘由已如前述，或者，此义应以相门之理来阐明。在此，以‘受’所摄取的五取蕴是苦谛；以‘受之集’所摄取的无明等是集谛；以灭尽和出离之说为灭谛；以‘如实知见’为道谛——如是，在此应知四圣谛。因为欲取是其余诸取之根本，并且，当欲取被断除时，就没有剩余的取了，因此说‘因离欲贪而无取’。‘无取解脱’是世尊显示其自身道果成就。法王以‘于诸受’等句，显示其一切知智连同前分道之生起处，因其善通达此法界，故能就有因、有去处、有差别地分析此见。
entries.english: By 'impermanent,' he speaks of the drawback of equanimous feeling by way of the suffering inherent in formations, or indeed of all feelings. By the other terms, he speaks of the drawback of painful and pleasant feelings respectively, by way of the other kinds of suffering. Or, without distinction, all three terms should be applied to all feelings. Here, the impermanent nature of feeling is its non-existence after having been; its suffering nature is its oppression by arising and passing away; and its liability to change in two ways, through aging and death—this is the drawback of feeling. Or, it is called a 'drawback' because supreme compassion proceeds from what is afflicted. In 'the escape from feeling,' the term 'from feeling' is a term for escape. As long as a person does not abandon the desire and lust bound up with feeling, they remain clinging to feeling. But when they abandon that desire and lust, they are freed and detached from feeling. Thus, the abandonment of desire and lust is called the escape from feeling. Here, by the taking up of 'feeling,' the material and immaterial phenomena that are co-nascent with, a support for, and an object of feeling are also included. Thus, the inclusion of all five aggregates of clinging should be understood. The teaching, however, is presented with feeling as the heading. The reason for this has already been stated, or this meaning should be analyzed by the method of extracting characteristics. In this context, the five aggregates of clinging, included by the taking up of 'feeling,' constitute the truth of suffering. Ignorance and so forth, included by the taking up of 'the origin of feelings,' constitute the truth of the origin. The truth of cessation is expressed through the terms 'passing away' and 'escape.' The truth of the path is indicated by the phrase 'having known as it really is.' Thus, the four truths should be understood here. Because sensual clinging is the root of the other clingings, and when sensual clinging is abandoned, the remaining clingings cease to exist, it is said, 'free from desire and lust, without clinging.' By 'freed through non-clinging,' the Blessed One here reveals his attainment of the path and fruit. By the phrase 'of feelings' and so on, the King of Dhamma shows the ground for the arising of his omniscience, together with the preliminary practice, on account of which, through having thoroughly penetrated a certain element of the Dhamma, he was able to analyze this view with its cause, its destination, and its divisions.

entries.pali: Atha vā evaṃ visesakāraṇato dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni vibhajitvā idāni avisesakāraṇato tāni dassetuṃ ‘‘tatra bhikkhave’’ tiādikā desanā āraddhā. Sabbesañhi diṭṭhigatikānaṃ vedanā avijjā taṇhā ca avisiṭṭhakāranti. Tattha tadapī ti ‘‘sassataṃ attānañca lokañca paññapenti’’ti ettha yadetaṃ ‘‘sassato attā ca loko cā’’ti paññāpanaṃ, tadapi. Sukhādibhedaṃ tividhavedayitaṃ yathākkamaṃ dukkhasallāniccato, avisesena samudayatthaṅgamassādādīnavanissaraṇato vā yathābhūtaṃ ajānantānaṃ apassantānaṃ, tato eva ca sukhādipatthanāsambhavato taṇhāya upagatattā taṇhāgatānaṃ taṇhāparitassitena diṭṭhivipphanditameva diṭṭhicalanameva, ‘‘asati attani ko vedanaṃ anubhavatī’’ti kāyavacīdvāresu diṭṭhiyā copanappattimattameva vā, na pana diṭṭhiyā paññāpetabbo sassato koci dhammo atthīti attho. Ekaccasassatavādādīsupi eseva nayo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 或者，在从特殊原因的角度分别解说六十二种见之后，现在为了从普遍原因的角度来开示它们，而开始了‘诸比丘’(bhikkhave)等教说。因为对于一切持见者，感受、无明与贪爱是其普遍的原因。其中，‘那也是’(tadapi)是指在‘宣示我与世界是常’之处，这‘我与世界是常’的宣示，也是如此。对于乐等三种感受，他们不如实知见其依次为苦、为箭、为无常，或不如实知见其集、灭、味、患、离，又因渴求乐等而为贪爱所行，由贪爱的焦灼所引起的，只是见的颤动(diṭṭhivipphandita)，只是见的摇动(diṭṭhicalana)而已。或者，那只是在身门与语门上，见的一种鼓动而已，即‘若无我，谁来感受？’，其义并非是通过见要宣示有某个常法存在。在一分常见论(ekaccasassatavāda)等中，也是此理。
entries.english: Alternatively, having thus divided the sixty-two views according to specific causes, the teaching beginning with “There, monks…” was started in order to now show them according to non-specific causes. For, for all who hold views, feeling, ignorance, and craving are the non-specific causes. Therein, “that also” refers to this proclamation, “the self and the world are eternal,” in the phrase “they proclaim the self and the world as eternal.” For those not knowing, not seeing as it truly is the threefold feeling divided into pleasure, etc., in accordance with the dart of suffering and impermanence respectively, or without distinction, according to arising, passing away, gratification, danger, and escape; and because of that, from the possibility of longing for pleasure, etc., for those who have gone to craving because they are overcome by craving, it is merely a throbbing of views agitated by craving, a stirring of views. Or it is merely the attainment of prompting by the view at the doors of body and speech, thinking, “If there is no self, who experiences feeling?” But there is no eternal phenomenon whatsoever to be proclaimed by a view; this is the meaning. The same principle applies also to the partial-eternalists and others.

entries.pali: Tattha ‘‘attā, loko’’ti ca diṭṭhiyā adhiṭṭhānabhāvena, vedanāphassāyatanādimukhena ca gahitesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu taṇhāvajjā pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhasaccaṃ. Taṇhā samudayasaccaṃ. Sā pana paritassanāggahaṇena ‘‘taṇhāgatāna’’nti, ‘‘vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’’ti ca sarūpeneva samudayaggahaṇena, bhavanettiggahaṇena ca pāḷiyaṃ gahitāva. Ayaṃ tāva suttantanayo. Abhidhammanayena pana āghātānandādivacanehi, ātappādipadehi, cittappadosavacanena, sabbadiṭṭhidīpakapadehi, kusalākusalaggahaṇena, bhavaggahaṇena, sokādiggahaṇena, tattha tattha samudayaggahaṇena cāti saṅkhepato sabbalokiyakusalākusaladhammavibhāvanapadehi gahitā kammakilesā samudayasaccaṃ. Ubhinnaṃ appavatti nirodhasaccaṃ. Tassa tattha tattha vedanānaṃ atthaṅgamanissaraṇapariyāyehi, paccattaṃ nibbutivacanena, anupādāvimuttivacanena ca pāḷiyaṃ gahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Nirodhapajānanā paṭipadā maggasaccaṃ. Tassāpi tattha tattha vedanānaṃ samudayādiyathābhūtavedanāpadesena, channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayādiyathābhūtapajānanapariyāyena, bhavanettiyā ucchedapariyāyena ca gahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tattha samudayena assādo, dukkhena ādīnavo, magganirodhehi nissaraṇa nti evaṃ catusaccavasena, yāni pāḷiyaṃ (netti. 9) sarūpeneva āgatāni assādādīnavanissaraṇāni, tesañca vasena idha assādādayo veditabbā. Vineyyānantādibhāvāpattiādikaṃ yathāvuttavibhāgaṃ payojanameva phalaṃ. Āghātādīnaṃ akaraṇīyatā, āghātādiphalassa ca anaññasantānabhāvitā, nindāpasaṃsāsu yathāsabhāvapaṭijānananibbeṭhanāti evaṃ taṃtaṃpayojanādhigamahetu upāyo. Āghātādīnaṃ karaṇapaṭisedhanādiapadesena dhammarājassa āṇatti veditabbāti ayaṃ desanāhāro.
entries.chinese_simplified: 其中，于作为“我”、“世间”等见的所依，并通过受、触、处等门所执取的五取蕴中，除去渴爱(taṇhā)的五取蕴即是苦圣谛。渴爱是集圣谛。此渴爱在圣典中，已通过在“为渴爱所至者[战栗]”中提及战栗、在“受缘渴爱”中提及自性、以及提及“有之导引”而被把握。这即是经藏的说法。然而，依阿毗达摩(Abhidhamma)之说，通过“嗔恚(āghāta)、喜悦(nandā)”等语，“热忱(ātappa)”等词，“心之恚害(cittappadosa)”之说，阐明一切见的词语，对善与不善的摄取，对有的摄取，对愁等的摄取，以及各处对集的摄取等——简言之，通过阐明一切世间善不善法的词语所摄取的业与烦恼，是集圣谛。此二者的不生起是灭圣谛。对于此，当知在圣典中，它是通过诸受的隐没、出离等方式，“各自寂灭”之说，以及“无取解脱”之说而被把握。了知灭的行道是道圣谛。对于此，亦当知在圣典中，它是通过对诸受的集起等如实了知的教示，对六触处的集起等如实了知的方式，以及对“有之导引”的断除方式而被把握。在此，集是味，苦是患，道与灭是离——如是依四圣谛，以及依圣典中(《导论》9)以其自性而来的味、患、离，当于此了知味等。所化者达到无量等状态，如前所述的区分，其作用即是果。不作嗔恚等，嗔恚等之果不生于他相续，于毁誉中如实辨明其自性——如是，达成彼彼作用之因即是方便。通过禁止作嗔恚等的教示，当知此是法王之教令。这便是教示要门。
entries.english: Here, the five aggregates subject to clinging are taken up as the basis for the view of "self, world," and by way of feeling, contact, sense bases, etc. These five aggregates subject to clinging, excluding craving, constitute the truth of suffering. Craving is the truth of origin. This craving is grasped in the texts by grasping agitation, by expressions like "those gone to craving (taṇhāgatāna)," "craving conditioned by feeling," by grasping origin in its own form, and by grasping the guide to becoming. This is the Suttanta method. In the Abhidhamma method, however, kamma and defilements are the truth of origin, grasped concisely by terms explaining all worldly wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, such as expressions of resentment and delight, terms like ardour, expressions of mental corruption, terms illuminating all views, the grasping of wholesome and unwholesome states, the grasping of becoming, the grasping of sorrow, etc., and by grasping origin in various places. The non-occurrence of both is the truth of cessation. Its grasping in the texts is to be understood through phrases about the passing away and escape from feelings, the expression of personal extinguishment, and the expression of liberation without clinging. The practice which is the understanding of cessation is the truth of the path. Its grasping is also to be understood through statements about the true knowledge of the origin, etc., of feelings, by way of the true knowledge of the origin, etc., of the six sense bases, and by way of the cutting off of the guide to becoming. Here, by way of the four truths, gratification is seen in the origin, danger in suffering, and escape in the path and cessation. These gratification, danger, and escape, which appear in the texts (Netti. 9) in their own form, should be understood accordingly. The purpose itself is the fruit, which, according to the aforementioned division, is the attainment of the final state and so on by those to be disciplined. The means for achieving that specific purpose is the non-doability of resentment, etc., the non-occurrence of the fruit of resentment, etc., in another's continuum, and the explanation of blame and praise by recognizing their true nature. The command of the King of Dhamma, given by way of prohibiting the doing of resentment, etc., should be understood. This is the Mode of Teaching.

entries.pali: Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgamātikāya pana atthato tāva – cattāro ti gaṇanaparicchedo, tena na tato heṭṭhā, na uddhanti dīpeti. Satipaṭṭhānā ti ettha dve satipaṭṭhānā satigocaropi satipi. ‘‘Catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmī’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 5.408) hi satigocaro ‘‘satipaṭṭhāna’’nti vuccati, tassattho patiṭṭhāti tasminti paṭṭhānaṃ, kā patiṭṭhāti? Sati. Satiyā paṭṭhānaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ . Padhānaṃ ṭhānanti vā paṭṭhānaṃ, satiyā paṭṭhānaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ . ‘‘Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.147) pana sati. Tassattho patiṭṭhātīti paṭṭhānaṃ, upaṭṭhāti okkantitvā pakkhanditvā pavattatīti attho. Satiyeva paṭṭhānatthena satipaṭṭhānaṃ . Atha vā saraṇaṭṭhena sati, sā ca upaṭṭhānaṭṭhena paṭṭhānanti satipaṭṭhānaṃ, idamidha adhippetaṃ. Yadi evaṃ, kasmā satipaṭṭhānāti bahuvacanaṃ kataṃ? Satiyā bahuttā. Ārammaṇabhedena hi bahukā tā satiyo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于《念处分别》本母之义，首先，‘四’是数量的限定(gaṇanaparicchedo)，由此显示其数量不过多亦不过少。于‘念处’(Satipaṭṭhāna)一词，有两种念处：念所缘(satigocara)与念(sati)本身。如在‘诸比丘，我将为你们宣说四念处的生起与灭没’等经文(相应部 5.408)中，念所缘被称为‘念处’。其义为：于彼处安立(patiṭṭhāti)，故为‘处’(paṭṭhāna)。什么安立？是念。念之处，故为‘念处’。或，‘处’(paṭṭhāna)即主要之所，念之主要之所，故为‘念处’。而在‘修习、多修四念处能圆满七觉支’等经文(中部 3.147)中，则指念本身。其义为：现起(upaṭṭhāti)，即进入、跃入而转起之义。正是念，以‘处’(paṭṭhāna)之义，而为‘念处’。又或，念有忆念(saraṇa)之义，而此念以现起(upaṭṭhāna)之义为‘处’(paṭṭhāna)，故为‘念处’；此即此处所意。若然，为何说‘念处’(satipaṭṭhānā)时用复数？因念有众多之故。确实，因所缘之差别，彼等念亦为众多。
entries.english: In the Mātikā of the Analysis of the Foundations of Mindfulness, first, as to the meaning of the terms—'four' denotes the numerical division, thereby indicating that there is nothing less nor more. As for `satipaṭṭhāna`—here, two aspects of `satipaṭṭhāna` are intended: the object of mindfulness and mindfulness itself. In passages such as, 'Monks, I shall teach the arising and passing away of the four foundations of mindfulness,' the object of mindfulness is called `satipaṭṭhāna`. Its meaning is 'establishment'—thus, `paṭṭhāna`. What is established? Mindfulness. The establishment of mindfulness is `satipaṭṭhāna`. Or, `paṭṭhāna` means 'principal place' or 'basis.' The foundation of mindfulness is `satipaṭṭhāna`. In passages such as, 'When the four foundations of mindfulness are developed and cultivated, they fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment,' mindfulness itself is meant by `satipaṭṭhāna`. Its meaning is 'establishment'—thus, `paṭṭhāna`, meaning it is present, enters into, and proceeds. Mindfulness itself, in the sense of foundation, is `satipaṭṭhāna`. Alternatively, mindfulness has the characteristic of recollection; and that is called `paṭṭhāna` by the meaning of being present—thus, `satipaṭṭhāna`. This is what is intended here. If so, why is `satipaṭṭhāna` used in the plural? Because of the multiplicity of mindfulness. For due to the diversity of objects, there are many instances of mindfulness.

entries.pali: Vissajjanā – sāvatthiyaṃ bhante sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha ‘‘dukkhassa bhikkhave samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmī’’ti evamādinā bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 答：尊者，是在舍卫城(Sāvatthī)，针对众多比丘而说。世尊以‘诸比丘，我将为你们开示苦的生起与灭尽。’等语开始宣说。
entries.english: Reply: At Sāvatthī, venerable sir, concerning a number of monks, the Blessed One spoke thus: "Monks, I will teach you the origination and the passing away of suffering."

entries.pali: Vissajjanā – rājagahe bhante sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha ‘‘yo hi koci vikkhave bhikkhu channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, avusitaṃ tena brahmacariyaṃ, ārakā so imasmā dhammavinayā’’ti evamādinā bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 答：尊者，在王舍城(Rājagaha)，世尊针对众多比丘说：‘诸比丘，若有比丘不如实了知六触处的集、灭、味、患、离，则其梵行未立，远离此法与律。’世尊如此宣说。
entries.english: Reply: At Rājagaha, venerable sir, concerning many bhikkhus, it was spoken by the Blessed One in this way, and so on: “Bhikkhus, any bhikkhu who does not understand as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to the six sense bases—the holy life has not been lived by him; he is far from this Dhamma and Discipline.”
